clue.text: Country bumpkin getting his teeth into pig-food

parts.note: chaw is a dialect form of chew, which is what you do when getting your teeth into food
bacon is food that comes from the pig

explanation.surface: A yokel tucks into a meal of pig swill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig-food' suggests swill fed to pigs, but here it is food made from a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English term of contempt for a rustic yokel, literally one who chews his bacon.

clue.text: Tree made from dried-up carbohydrate?

indicators.note: something made from material reshapes it, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dried up means the water, the hydrate part of the word, has been removed

explanation.surface: A tree grown from dehydrated starch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dried-up' removes HYDRATE from CARBOHYDRATE, leaving CARBO, which 'made from' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean evergreen whose pods are used as a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Commend a super-soft archbishop

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is very soft in music
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: Praise a very gentle churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to praise or commend.

clue.text: Account includes a rate change for a couple of parties

indicators.note: one piece takes the others into its middle

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed

indicators.note: change means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An invoice that shows a revised rate for two sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral agreements involve two sides, each a party to the deal.

clue.text: Scrap Rugby Union clue — terribly dim

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Throw away a rugby clue that is awfully obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepuscular means of twilight, so dim and half-lit.

clue.text: Forty Winks is specially recommended

explanation.surface: A short sleep is advised.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sleep; and a racing tipster's strongest selection, a horse specially tipped.

clue.text: Zulu chief gives honour to an Egyptian genius

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
in ancient Egyptian belief the ka is a person's spiritual double or guardian genius

explanation.surface: A Zulu king pays tribute to a brilliant Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genius' looks like a clever person but means a guardian spirit, the Egyptian ka.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Zulu kingdom in the early nineteenth century, more often spelt Shaka.

clue.text: She indicates one is out of vehicle lubricant

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: out of means taken away from the longer piece

parts.note: oil is a lubricant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman points out her motor needs oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for a female person.

clue.text: Natal city of 5 at length

parts.note: 5 down's answer, written out at full length, becomes the name of the French emperor; natal means of birth, so this is his birthplace in Corsica

explanation.surface: A South African city linked to clue 5.
explanation.walkthrough: Natal is not the South African province: it means of one's birth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Corsican capital where Bonaparte was born in 1769.

clue.text: Fair, if relatively shy, type

parts.note: a fairground figure; relatively points to a family member, and a shy is a throw at a target

explanation.surface: A pretty but rather timid sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: A shy is a throw at a fairground target: the figure is a fairground game, a wooden woman's head pelted with sticks or balls, also anyone who attracts unfair criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground dummy at which players throw sticks, and so an easy target of criticism.

clue.text: Battle cruiser giving engineers beans perhaps

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
beans are an example of pulse, edible seeds of legumes

explanation.surface: A warship's crew is fed beans by the engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Repulse was a Royal Navy battlecruiser, sunk off Malaya in 1941.

clue.text: Relate saucy article in conclusion

parts.note: saucy means cheeky, pert
A is the indefinite article
the word in itself, placed at the conclusion of the answer

explanation.surface: Tell a story about a cheeky item at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain to something is to relate or belong to it.

clue.text: Note final expletive

parts.note: B is a musical note
final means last

explanation.surface: A last swear word to close the message.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of annoyance, a mild curse uttered when things go wrong.

clue.text: Liberal backing in high-class music arrangement is somewhat omphalic

definitions.note: an adjective phrase for a noun: the thing that is to do with the navel

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the other
a musical arrangement reorders, so these letters are rearranged
backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation is read right to left

explanation.surface: A posh musical arrangement with liberal leanings sounds rather navel-gazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' rearranges U and MUSIC; 'backing' turns LIB into BIL, which goes 'in' among them. Omphalic means relating to the navel.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel is the medical Latin word's meaning, and omphalic means navel-related.

clue.text: A good big car? Could be boasting

indicators.note: could be signals the letters can be reformed into another word

explanation.surface: A fine large car could be showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty boasting, from a vainglorious character in Spenser's Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Very inferior German spa

explanation.surface: A German health resort that is truly second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad means of poor quality, and in German names Bad marks a spa town, as in Baden-Baden or Bad Ems.

clue.text: Prominent croppers in the deer park

definitions.text: Prominent croppers in the deer park

parts.words: Prominent croppers in the deer park
parts.note: croppers are teeth that crop grass; a male deer in a park would have them, and protruding front teeth carry that name

explanation.surface: Grazing animals stand out in a deer park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Croppers' suggests grazing animals; it means teeth, and a male deer gives the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper front teeth that stick out, named after the male deer.

clue.text: Music is sweet, that is sticky, if amusing

parts.note: rock is a sticky stick of seaside sweet
an is an archaic word for if
droll means amusing

explanation.surface: A tune is like candy: gooey, but funny.
explanation.walkthrough: AN for 'if' is old usage, as in Shakespeare's 'an it please you'. Rock is a hard sugary stick sold at British seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of popular dance music that began in the 1950s.

clue.text: Decide to finish

explanation.surface: Make up one's mind to end it.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a matter; and, in old and legal usage, to bring to an end.

clue.text: By which one might reach Babylon

definitions.text: By which one might reach Babylon

parts.words: By which one might reach Babylon
parts.note: the nursery rhyme 'How many miles to Babylon?' asks whether one can get there by the glow of a wax taper, and is told yes, and back again

explanation.surface: A question of how to travel to the ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The light of a wax taper, the means of travel the old nursery rhyme names for the trip.

clue.text: "So shines a good deed in a —— world" (Mer. of Venice)

definitions.text: "So shines a good deed in a —— world" (Mer. of Venice)

parts.words: "So shines a good deed in a —— world" (Mer. of Venice)
parts.note: Portia's line in The Merchant of Venice, comparing a small candle's light to a kind act in a wicked world

explanation.surface: A gap in a line from Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Here it carries its old sense of wicked, not just mischievous.

clue.text: Permissive flower girl

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded girl who loves blossoms.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it grants permission; it is also hawthorn blossom, and a girl's name.

clue.text: One item raised into 1,100 — by copying

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other

parts.note: M is Roman 1,000 and C is Roman 100

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means turned upward, read bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the word item, taken as written

explanation.surface: An item put into a large number by imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses the run ONE ITEM, giving IMETI, which goes 'into' MC.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimetic means imitative, given to mimicry.

clue.text: Clapped liked the cannons in Death Valley ?

definitions.text: liked the cannons in Death Valley

explanation.surface: Applauded the guns in an American desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Death Valley is not the Californian desert: in Tennyson's 'Charge of the Light Brigade' the six hundred ride into the valley of Death, where the cannon 'volley'd and thunder'd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder claps; and in Tennyson's poem the guns roared at the cavalry.

clue.text: These are due to the way to bed being upstairs

indicators.note: in a down clue upstairs means going upward, so the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bills to pay because the bedroom is upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owed is money due to be paid.

clue.text: Weird Burma dance

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are turned into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A strange dance from Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance in quick rhythm.

clue.text: Cancel one of two articles in the year-book

definitions.text: Cancel one of two articles in the year-book

indicators.note: cancel means strike out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: an annual is a book issued once a year
the word holds two As, and A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Strike out one of a pair of pieces in the yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: annulling is cancelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void, to cancel.

clue.text: Show produced at court

explanation.surface: Evidence displayed in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To display; and an object brought out as evidence in a trial.

clue.text: On which the Treasury issues watered stock?

definitions.text: On which the Treasury issues watered stock?

parts.words: On which the Treasury issues watered stock?
parts.note: Treasury bills on sale continuously are said to be issued on this; it also lets out water

explanation.surface: A question about government finance and diluted shares.
explanation.walkthrough: Watered stock is shares diluted in value; here it is water from a faucet. Government stock sold continuously is a 'tap' issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A faucet issues water, and government stock on continuous sale is on this.

clue.text: Something elevating in study at public school

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to con is to study, as in conning a script
a lift raises people, so it is something elevating

explanation.surface: Uplifting reading time at a private boarding school.
explanation.walkthrough: Clifton College is a well-known independent (British 'public') school in Bristol.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English fee-paying boarding school in Bristol, named for the suburb.

clue.text: Where visibility sounds poor in Greater London

indicators.note: sounds means the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: a haze is mist where visibility is poor

explanation.surface: A London district where it is hard to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Hayes is a suburb of west London, near Heathrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A district in the borough of Hillingdon, on the western edge of the capital.

clue.text: "Dance and —— song, and sunburnt mirth!" (Keats)

parts.note: a line from Keats's Ode to a Nightingale, describing the songs of the south of France

explanation.surface: A gap in a line of Keats's poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wishes for wine tasting of the southern French region, its dancing and songs.
